summary: The /settings page has no client-side step-up handler for its htmx forms, so an MFA-enrolled operator with an expired proof sees the API-token Create and Revoke buttons do nothing. The two existing user-management step-up buttons on the same page share the shape. Also raised downstream as UP-2 and ER-2 (echoes).

classification_rationale: Filed as #6003 (owner approved filing, 2026-10-17). Disclosed in the Breaking changelog fragment and the upgrade note; the refusal itself is correct and nothing is mutated.

summary: Dashboard enrollment-token routes carry no step-up check and have no REST v1 twin. Pre-existing, outside this change.

The step-up route list in rest-api.md and the token rows in server-admin.md omit the two newly gated dashboard routes. Fixed in 6309ad34f. The report also claimed the Settings page shares the console's global step-up handler; checked and wrong (kDashJs8 is only in dashboard_ui.cpp), which is why SG-1 stands.
Fragment wording overstated ('wherever') and carried an internal ledger sentence. Reworded in 6309ad34f and again in be4cfb9a4.

The count of step-up-gated endpoints disagrees across authentication.md (26), server-admin.md and auth-architecture.md (24); also raised as ER-3. Pre-existing drift, widened by two routes. Not touched.
The ADR-1005 settings-plane exception table still lists both token routes; it is a historical inventory and is treated the same way for other twinned routes. No change.
classification_rationale: Historical inventory; the table is not a live ledger.

trigger: A dashboard mint with a tier chosen; a tier with no TTL; the token store closed.
summary: Flipping the two ledger rows to twinned overstated equivalence with the REST v1 twins: the create success audit lacked the tier detail, an MCP-tier token with no TTL or over 90 days was reported as an entropy failure, and the dashboard dereferenced the token store without an availability check. Fixed in 6309ad34f, verified closed by the architect, the consistency-auditor and the security-guardian in the Gate 8 pass.
classification_rationale: Native SHOULD; the I6 false-assurance reading of 'twinned' derives HIGH.

summary: The first tests did not prove the step-up gate runs before form validation and the id lookup. Added a gate-ordering test in 6309ad34f and an extra MCP-tier body in e0920e4d1.

No assertion that a refused step-up writes no audit row. These handlers audit through audit_store_, which is null in the harness, so the assertion would be vacuous; the refusal row is written by require_mfa_step_up (stubbed here). Also raised by compliance as a NICE.
classification_rationale: Vacuous in this harness; the quality-engineer agreed in the Gate 8 pass.

summary: The new store-unavailable 503 guard on both routes had no test. Added in e0920e4d1 (needs no Postgres).

No route-level test drives the real require_mfa_step_up 401 envelope, and the success audit tier detail is untested because audit_store_ is null in the harness. The two existing user-management step-up sites share the gap.
The DELETE test accepts either a hard-delete or a revoked flag. Deliberate: the store behaviour is revoke-or-remove.

The new TTL and tier refusal spans return HTTP 200, so htmx swaps them into #api-token-section and replaces the table and form until reload. The other validation spans in the same handler already behave this way.

SAML sessions are refused with 403 on both routes, as on the REST token routes, so SAML-only operators lose Settings-page token create and revoke. Consistent with the v1 twins. Disclosed in the Breaking changelog fragment, the upgrade note and the SAML step-up paragraphs; the supported alternative (an API-token or MCP caller, or a local or OIDC administrator) is named.

classification_rationale: Documented in be4cfb9a4 (changelog.d fragment moved to changed with a Breaking lead, docs/user-manual/upgrading.md, authentication.md, server-admin.md). Raised independently by unhappy-path, docs-writer, consistency-auditor and enterprise-readiness (and the emergency-revocation angle by compliance-officer).

trigger: Postgres pool exhaustion or a database error during a token create.
summary: Any create_token failure other than the TTL and tier cases fixed here (pool timeout, database error text, a shutdown race) still reaches the shared failure branch and is reported as an entropy failure: 503, yuzu_secure_random_failure_total, and a csprng_unavailable audit row. Shared with POST /api/v1/tokens and MCP create_api_token. This change strictly narrows the reachable set on the dashboard path.

classification_rationale: Owner: Dave Rae (maintainer). Decision 2026-10-17, asked in this session: defer, and file or link a tracking issue. The existing open issue #2175 (typed create_token error) already covers it, so the evidence was added there as a comment instead of filing a duplicate. Risk accepted by the owner, not independently adjudicated; the owner is also the change author. Interim: no shipped alert keys on the counter (sre), so the misdirection reaches the audit row and any operator-authored rule. #2175 carries no priority or triage label yet; that is open. This stays the one unresolved HIGH-derived item and is flagged in the PR body.
waiver_rationale: Pre-existing, shared with the v1 and MCP twins, strictly narrowed by this change, and the full fix is a typed error spanning the store and three callers (tracked in #2175).

summary: The tier/TTL rule now exists in three places (the store, rest_api_v1.cpp, the dashboard) with no shared constant. The typed error in #2175 would remove both handler copies.
classification_rationale: Native LOW; the reporter's facts (I3) derive HIGH, mapped BLOCKING. Pre-existing and the same defect class as sa-UP-6; covered by the same owner decision and the same issue (#2175).

summary: revoke_token returns true for an already-revoked row, so a repeated or concurrent revoke records another success audit row; the same on the REST DELETE. Pre-existing and outside this change; no issue filed yet (owner to say whether to file).
classification_rationale: Native MEDIUM; the reporter's facts (I3) derive HIGH, mapped BLOCKING. Pre-existing and shared with the REST DELETE. NOT covered by the sa-UP-6 decision: needs its own owner decision (file an issue, or accept). Unresolved HIGH-derived item.

summary: The new store-unavailable 503 set no error toast, unlike the adjacent 503 branches. Fixed in e0920e4d1.

The twinned rows hid four asymmetries (no scope_service, ttl_hours versus expires_at, audit rows without user-agent, principal-class and session-id stamps, no MCP step-up). Recorded as a known-asymmetry paragraph in the ledger doc in e0920e4d1. The missing audit stamps are a pre-existing gap with no issue.
An empty token name on POST /api/v1/tokens and MCP create_api_token reaches the entropy-failure branch, the same mislabelling class as UP-6. Pre-existing in the siblings.
classification_rationale: Native NICE; the reporter's facts (I3) derive HIGH, mapped BLOCKING. Pre-existing sibling of sa-UP-6 on the REST and MCP create paths; covered by the same owner decision and issue (#2175).

summary: The recipe says ApiToken:Write is absent from requires_approval(); mcp_policy.hpp includes it. Pre-existing doc drift, not touched.

The changelog fragment told every operator to sign in again, which cannot work for SAML (refused unconditionally), and did not state that SAML operators lose dashboard token create and revoke. Fixed in e0920e4d1, then moved to the changed section with a Breaking lead in be4cfb9a4.

classification_rationale: e0920e4d1 rewrote the fragment; be4cfb9a4 added the Breaking lead, the upgrade note and the SAML step-up paragraph sentences. Also raised by the consistency-auditor (F1).

summary: The change newly refuses a session class, so it needs a Breaking lead in the changed section and an upgrade note. Fixed in be4cfb9a4.
A SAML-only operator has no session-based revoke path during an incident; the fragment did not name the supported emergency route. Added to the fragment and the upgrade note in be4cfb9a4.

Dashboard audit rows (written through AuditStore::log directly) lack the user-agent, principal-class and session-id stamps the REST and MCP rows carry. Pre-existing; this change does not worsen it. Recorded in the ledger doc; no tracking issue filed yet.
yuzu_secure_random_failure_total is not in the metrics catalogue and no shipped rule uses it. Pre-existing; not required for this change.
